_readme: Reviewed judgements for the recommendation eval. This file is the only real
quality signal in the eval: the `keywords` list in recommendation-eval.mjs is a
loose substring floor that scored 100% on a run that answered 'TLDR' for 'find
and fix bugs in my codebase'.
IMPORTANT: every entry below is labeledBy 'assistant' — these are Claude's
judgements from reviewing one collected run, NOT human labels. The eval reports
the human-reviewed count separately for exactly that reason. Flip labeledBy to
'human' as you confirm each one; that number is the acceptance criterion for
'recommendations are genuinely useful', and it is currently 0.
Fields (all optional):
acceptTools  names that are a correct answer; non-empty means the best match
MUST be one of them. Deliberately EMPTY in this seed except where
one product really is the canonical answer — pinning accepts to
whatever was returned today would make every future improvement
register as a failure.
rejectTools  answers judged wrong. A hit is reported as a REGRESSION, because
it means something a reviewer already rejected came back.
requireAll   every term must appear in the best match's name+description+tags.
requireAny   at least one must appear. Tighter than the loose `keywords` list.
notes        why the judgement went the way it did.
Regenerate the review material with:
node scripts/eval/recommendation-eval.mjs http://localhost:3000 --collect
_policy: DECIDED 2026-09-10 by the project owner: a GitHub repository or demo app IS an
acceptable answer. It does not have to be a hosted commercial product.
Consequence for labelling: 'this is a repo, not a product' is NOT a reason to
reject on its own. Judge the repo on whether it does the job the goal asks for.
A repo can still be rejected for an ordinary reason — for instance requiring a
command line when the goal explicitly says 'without coding'.
This decision resolves the open question that was flagged against
'build a chatbot trained on my own documents'.

labels.query: turn my podcast into short clips
labels.notes: Klipme fits the goal. Accepting on intent terms rather than pinning the name, since several clip tools would be equally right.

labels.query: generate product photos for my online store
labels.notes: Tightened from the loose list: bare 'image' or 'photo' would pass any image generator, which is not the same as product photography.

labels.query: write blog posts for my company
labels.notes: Writepaw fits. Broad intent terms are acceptable here because the goal itself is broad.

labels.query: transcribe interview recordings to text
labels.notes: Dropped bare 'audio' and 'text' from the loose list — both match tools that have nothing to do with transcription.

labels.query: build a website without coding
labels.notes: THE LABEL WAS WRONG, not the system. It failed 'ai-website-builder', whose description literally says 'no coding required' — the term list had 'no code' but not 'no coding'. Added both phrasings; that answer is correct. ai-website-cloner-template stays rejected, but NOT for being a repo (see _policy): its own description is 'clone any website with one command using AI coding', which is disqualifying for a goal that says without coding.

labels.query: remove the background from images
labels.notes: Background remover AI is a direct hit.

labels.query: help me write code faster
labels.notes: REJECT: screenshot-to-code is one narrow task, not general coding speed. The right answers are inline-completion assistants. Note this same tool IS correct for the screenshot query below — the miss is intent matching, not the catalog.

labels.query: create a logo for my brand
labels.notes: Logopony is a direct hit. Removed bare 'design' and 'graphic' from the loose list as too permissive.

labels.query: summarize long research papers
labels.notes: Article Summarizer is acceptable but weak — the goal says research papers (PDFs, citations) and an article summarizer is a near neighbour, not the same thing. Worth revisiting if a paper-specific tool exists in the catalog.

labels.query: make an explainer video from a script
labels.notes: Luma AI passes on 'text to video' but is a generative clip model, not an explainer-video builder. Accepted weakly; a reviewer may well downgrade this.

labels.query: answer customer support questions automatically
labels.notes: Quickchat AI fits.

labels.query: translate my documents into other languages
labels.notes: DeepL Translate is the canonical answer, but acceptTools is left empty on purpose so other real translators still pass.

labels.query: analyze my spreadsheet data
labels.notes: REJECT: DATAGEN generates synthetic data; the goal is analyzing data the user already has. Opposite direction of the same noun.

labels.query: schedule and post to social media
labels.notes: Magicpost fits.

labels.query: detect whether text was written by AI
labels.notes: DetectGPT is a direct hit.

labels.query: practice for a job interview
labels.notes: InterviewBot fits. Dropped 'resume' from the loose list — a resume builder does not let you practise.

labels.query: clean up and enhance old photos
labels.notes: MediaChance's enhancer fits. Dropped bare 'photo'/'image', which match every image tool in the catalog.

labels.query: build a chatbot trained on my own documents
labels.notes: Repo policy resolved (see _policy): Robby-chatbot is acceptable. Its description — 'chat with CSV, PDF, TXT files using Langchain' — is genuinely document-grounded chat, and the term list simply missed that canonical phrasing, so pdf/csv/'chat with' are now included. THIS QUERY STILL FAILS, and correctly: the current best match is SiteGPT, which trains on 'the content of your website', not on documents you supply. The right answer was already in its own alternatives — Whismer, 'train these chatbots by uploading documents', tagged knowledge base + document upload. Retrieval found it; ranking put it third. That is a ranking bug, not a catalog gap.

labels.query: generate music for my video project
labels.notes: Music AI fits.

labels.query: automate repetitive tasks between my apps
labels.notes: REJECT: Jotform is form-building with agents bolted on; the goal is app-to-app integration (Zapier/Make/n8n territory). 'Automat' alone in the loose list is what let this through.

labels.query: help me study for an exam
labels.notes: REJECT: 'Academic Help' is a generic essay/homework service, not a study aid — and it was the one answer the loose keyword check also flagged, which is why it is worth encoding properly.

labels.query: edit my video by typing instead of timelines
labels.notes: REJECT: Videoleap is a conventional timeline editor, which is precisely what the query asked to avoid. The loose list passed it on 'video' + 'edit'.

labels.query: find and fix bugs in my codebase
labels.notes: REJECT: TLDR is a summarizer. This is the case that motivated the whole labels file — the loose check passed it because 'code' appeared somewhere in the description.

labels.query: turn a screenshot into working code
labels.notes: Screenshot Coder is a direct hit — the correct home for this tool, unlike the 'write code faster' query above.

labels.query: write cold outreach emails that convert
labels.notes: AllWrite is a general writing tool and fails these terms, which is the intended outcome: the goal is sales outreach, not prose. The 'maybe it is a catalog gap' caveat is now answered — it is not. ContentEdge, tagged 'sales copy' + 'email' + 'marketers', sits in the same result set as an alternative, so again retrieval found something better and ranking preferred the generic writer. Same shape as 'build a chatbot trained on my own documents'.

labels.query: generate voiceovers for my videos
labels.notes: Ankara AI could not be judged from its catalog entry alone — the name says nothing about voice. Left with intent terms so the check is meaningful, but this one genuinely needs a human to look at the product.
